simple: One thing that can be only 0 or 1.
analogy: One light switch, either off or on.
precise: a binary digit; the smallest unit of information, holding exactly one of two values, written 0 and 1.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-20)

simple: A way of writing numbers with only two symbols, 0 and 1.
analogy: A row of switches where each one is worth double the one to its right.
precise: the base-2 place-value number system; each position is worth a power of two.
source: W1 of F0-20; D2 §2.1 of F0-20 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-20)

simple: How many different digit symbols a number system uses.
analogy: How many positions each switch (or dial) has.
precise: the number of distinct digits in a place-value system, and the factor by which each position's value grows to the left: 10 for decimal, 2 for binary.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-20)

simple: How much a digit is worth because of where it sits.
analogy: The number Lina wrote above each switch.
precise: the weight of a position in a number; in base 2 the positions from the right are worth 1, 2, 4, 8, … (each a power of two). You met place value for decimal numbers in F0-11.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-20)

simple: What happens when a number is too big for the switches you have.
analogy: Trying to show 8 with only three switches: there is no switch worth 8, so the row goes back to all off.
precise: the result of a calculation needs more bits than the storage has; the extra high bits are lost and the stored value wraps around.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-20)

simple: The everyday way of writing numbers with the ten digits 0 to 9.
analogy: A dial with ten positions instead of a switch with two.
precise: the base-10 place-value number system; each position is worth ten times the one to its right.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-21)

simple: The bit on the far right, worth 1.
analogy: The switch at the right end of the hallway, the one that flips most often.
precise: the bit with the smallest place value, 2 = 1; it decides whether the number is odd (1) or even (0).
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-21)

simple: The bit on the far left, worth the most.
analogy: The switch at the left end, the one with the biggest number written above it.
precise: the bit with the largest place value in a number of a given width; in 8 bits it is worth 2 = 128.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-21)

simple: What is left over after sharing out equally.
analogy: Sharing buttons between two jars: if one button is left over, the remainder is 1.
precise: for whole numbers, n = 2 × q + r with r equal to 0 or 1 when dividing by 2; in C++ the operator % gives the remainder and / between whole numbers gives the whole-number quotient q.
source: W1 of F0-21; R1 of F0-21 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-21)

simple: A way of writing numbers with sixteen symbols: 0 to 9, then A to F.
analogy: A one-symbol nickname for every group of four hallway switches.
precise: the base-16 place-value system; the digits A–F stand for 10–15, and each position is worth 16 times the one to its right.
source: W1 of F0-22; R1 of F0-22 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-22)

simple: One symbol of a hexadecimal number.
analogy: The nickname for one group of four switches.
precise: one of the sixteen symbols 0–9, A–F; it stands for exactly four bits, because 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-22)

simple: Half of a row of eight bits: four bits.
analogy: One group of four switches.
precise: a group of 4 bits; one hex digit writes one nibble. This course uses the word with exactly this meaning.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-22)

simple: A label in front of a number that says "this is written in hex".
analogy: A sticky note on the row saying "read me with nicknames".
precise: the prefix 0x marks a hexadecimal literal in C++ (for example 0x2A is 42); this university also writes hex as 0x2A in running text (guide 13.3).
source: R1 of F0-22; D2 §5.13.2 of F0-22 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-22)

simple: A group of eight bits.
analogy: One row of eight hallway switches, each worth double the one to its right.
precise: a group of 8 bits that holds one of 256 patterns (0 to 255 when read as an unsigned number); the unit symbol is B. The C++ constant CHAR_BIT printed 8 in our run.
source: W1 of F0-23; R1 of F0-23; D3 of F0-23 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-23)

simple: The size of number a computer likes to work with in one go.
analogy: How many rows of switches the house's control panel flips at once.
precise: a machine-dependent group of bytes that a processor handles as one unit; its size is set by the processor's architecture manual, not by a universal rule.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-23)

simple: One thousand bytes.
analogy: Ana's box of 1000 cookies.
precise: 1 kB = 1000 B, using the decimal (SI) prefix kilo = 10; MB = 1000 B, GB = 1000 B.
source: W1 of F0-23; D2 §3 of F0-23 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-23)

simple: 1024 bytes.
analogy: Felix's box of 1024 cookies.
precise: 1 KiB = 2 B = 1024 B, using the binary prefix kibi; MiB = 1024 B, GiB = 1024 B.
source: W1 of F0-23; D3 of F0-23 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-23)

simple: Small b means bits, capital B means bytes.
analogy: One switch versus one whole row.
precise: 1 B = 8 bit. The standard symbol for the byte is B; the bit is written "bit" in standard symbols (for example 1 kbit = 1000 bit), and many documents shorten it to a small b. This university spells out "Gbit/s" and "GB/s" at levels L0–L2 so the two cannot be mixed up (guide 13.3).
source: W1 of F0-23; D3 of F0-23 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-23)

simple: A number that can never be below zero.
analogy: The bicycle counter read plainly: 000 to 999.
precise: an integer type whose bit pattern is read with all place values positive; with 8 bits it holds 0 to 255. In C++, std::uint8_t is an unsigned 8-bit type.
source: R1 of F0-24; D2 §17.4.1 of F0-24 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-24)

simple: A number that can be negative or positive.
analogy: The counter read with Jonas's agreement: 999 means −1.
precise: an integer type that can represent negative values; in C++, std::int8_t is a signed 8-bit type holding −128 to 127.
source: R1 of F0-24; D2 §6.8.1 of F0-24 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-24)

simple: The usual rule for writing negative numbers in binary.
analogy: Going backwards from 000 on the counter.
precise: an n-bit representation where the most significant bit has place value −2 and all others are positive; −x is written as the pattern of 2 − x, found by inverting all bits of x and adding 1.
source: W1 of F0-24; D3 §2.1 of F0-24; D2 §6.8.1 of F0-24 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-24)

simple: The leftmost bit, which tells you if a signed number is negative.
analogy: The leftmost switch, now worth −128 instead of +128.
precise: in two's complement, the most significant bit; it is 1 exactly when the value is negative.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-24)

simple: Going past the end of the numbers and coming back at the other end.
analogy: The counter going from 999 to 000, or from 000 back to 999.
precise: arithmetic modulo 2: a result that does not fit in n bits keeps only its low n bits. It is one form of overflow (F0-20).
source: W1 of F0-24; R1 of F0-24 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-24)

simple: The name of a bit's position, counted from the right, starting at 0.
analogy: The room number of each switch on Zara's panel: kitchen is 0, garden is 7.
precise: bit k has place value 2; bit 0 is the least significant bit and bit 7 the most significant bit of a byte.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-25)

simple: A pattern of bits that picks which bits you want to touch.
analogy: The card with holes over some switches.
precise: a value combined with data by a bitwise operator so that only the bit positions selected by the mask are set, cleared, toggled or kept.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-25)

simple: An operation that works on each pair of bits separately.
analogy: Doing the same thing to every switch at once, switch by switch.
precise: in C++, & (AND: 1 only if both bits are 1), | (OR: 1 if at least one is 1), ^ (XOR: 1 if they differ) and ~ (NOT: flip every bit). F0-26 gives their full truth tables.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-25)

simple: Sliding all the bits left or right by some places.
analogy: Moving every light's setting a few rooms along the panel; settings that fall off the end are lost, and empty places get "off".
precise: x << n moves the bits of x n places left (multiplying an unsigned value by 2 while it fits); x >> n moves them n places right (dividing an unsigned value by 2, dropping the remainder).
source: W1 of F0-25; R1 of F0-25; D2 §7.6.7 of F0-25 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-25)

simple: One bit that answers a yes/no question.
analogy: One light: on means yes.
precise: a single bit in a larger value whose 1 or 0 records whether a condition is true.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-25)

simple: A group of neighbouring bits that together hold a small number.
analogy: Three switches side by side used as a dial from 0 to 7.
precise: a contiguous range of bits within a value, read by shifting it down to bit 0 and masking off the other bits.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-25)

simple: A value that is either true or false.
analogy: A switch is on or off; a lamp is lit or dark.
precise: a value of a two-element set {false, true}, written 0 and 1; in C++ the type bool, which prints as 0 or 1 by default (run R1).
source: R1 of F0-26; D4 §1.1.1 of F0-26; D3 §6.8.1 of F0-26 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-26)

simple: A table that lists every possible input and the output for each.
analogy: A chart by the cupboard that says, for each position of the two switches, whether the light is on.
precise: a complete listing of a Boolean function: one row for each of the 2 combinations of its n inputs, with the output value.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-26)

simple: True only when both inputs are true.
analogy: Two switches one after the other in the same wire (in series).
precise: the Boolean function with output 1 exactly when all inputs are 1; in C++, && for bool values and & bit by bit (F0-25).
source: W1 of F0-26; R1 of F0-26 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-26)

simple: True when at least one input is true.
analogy: Two switches side by side (in parallel): either one can light the lamp.
precise: the Boolean function with output 1 when one or more inputs are 1; in C++, || and bitwise |. It is "inclusive": both on also gives 1.
source: W1 of F0-26; R1 of F0-26 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-26)

simple: Turns true into false and false into true.
analogy: A push button that breaks the circuit while you press it.
precise: the one-input Boolean function with output equal to the opposite of the input; in C++, ! and bitwise ~.
source: W1 of F0-26; R1 of F0-26 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-26)

simple: True when the two inputs are different.
analogy: The stair light: flipping either switch changes the lamp.
precise: the two-input Boolean function with output 1 exactly when the inputs differ; for bool values in C++, a != b, and bitwise ^.
source: W1 of F0-26; R1 of F0-26 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-26)

simple: Rules for rewriting true/false sentences, like the rules for rewriting sums.
analogy: Tidying the house rules on the fridge without changing what they mean.
precise: the algebra of the values 0 and 1 with the operations AND, OR and NOT, and the laws they satisfy; named after the mathematician George Boole.
source: W1 of F0-27; D1 ch. 6 of F0-27 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-27)

simple: A rule written with letters, AND, OR, NOT and brackets.
analogy: "NOT (door open OR window open)" written short as NOT (D OR W).
precise: a formula built from Boolean variables, the constants 0 and 1, the operators AND, OR, NOT and brackets; it has one output value for each combination of variable values.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-27)

simple: Two rules that always give the same answer.
analogy: Two ways of saying the same house rule.
precise: two Boolean expressions are equivalent when their outputs agree in every row of their truth table.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-27)

simple: One case that shows a claim is wrong.
analogy: One open window under a green light.
precise: an assignment of input values for which two expressions claimed equal give different outputs; one counterexample is enough to disprove equivalence.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-27)

simple: To push a NOT inside a bracket, flip each part and swap AND with OR.
analogy: "not (open door or open window)" means "closed door and closed window".
precise: NOT (A AND B) = (NOT A) OR (NOT B), and NOT (A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B); named after the mathematician Augustus De Morgan.
source: W1 of F0-27; R1 of F0-27; D1 ch. 6 of F0-27; D5 of F0-27 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-27)

simple: A sentence about a process that stays true at every step.
analogy: "the two jars together hold twenty marbles", whatever moves are made.
precise: a condition (a Boolean expression about the state, F0-27) that holds in the starting state and is preserved by every allowed step, so it holds in every state reached.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-28)

simple: An invariant for a repeating part of a program.
analogy: The marble total checked after every turn of the game.
precise: a condition that is true before a loop starts and remains true after each pass of the loop body; together with the loop's stopping condition it proves what the loop computes.
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-28)

simple: Whether a number is odd or even.
analogy: Whether the marbles can be paired off with none left over.
precise: the remainder of a whole number after dividing by 2: 0 (even) or 1 (odd); for a binary number it is the least significant bit (F0-21).
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-28)

simple: A line in a program that tests the invariant and complains if it is false.
analogy: Counting all the marbles after each turn.
precise: code that evaluates the invariant at chosen points and reports a failure; in larger C++ programs this can be written with assert (introduced in later courses).
source: R1 of F0-28; D2 §19.3 of F0-28 (verification pass 2026-10-10)
last_verified: 2026-10-10 (verification pass; see the dossier of F0-28)
